Tips for Alice (Grunt, gpt-6-luna): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- A visit shows only a destination, not the action or alignment: a track or watch can't tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. Killing an attacker at night doesn't cancel their attack that same night. (seen in 2 games)
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads. Accusing someone and then voting No or Innocent on them is exactly the mismatch Vigilantes shoot.
- Watch for a player who stays quiet for days and then suddenly makes a concrete accusation right as the board changes, such as just after a flip. The timing of the pivot is the tell.
- Private messages are publicly visible, so briefly summarize yours in public. Before accusing someone from the record, re-check who sent each PM, each vote, and the exact wording of results; one reversed fact can sink a true claimant.

## Village
- When two Sheriff claimants call each other Evil, both can be telling the truth, because Executioners and Jesters read Evil. Don't hang on who sounded better; wait a day or find a mechanical check. (seen in 2 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording, delays or empty results (a blocked investigator has nothing to report). Before a hang, name what separates a lie from an honest mistake, a frame or a Roleplayer. (seen in 2 games)
- Ask every living player to name a strongest suspect with reasons each day. Repeated 'no case' answers give evil cover, while named reads build a record to check against later flips. (seen in 2 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or its tokens early, and never announce tonight's investigation target; announcements got investigators blocked or killed. Put your info in your last will and post only resolved results. (seen in 2 games)
- Track PM clusters and voting blocs across trials. Innocent votes alongside a flipped Yakuza, or PMs from them, outweigh a late unverifiable claim like Roleplayer.
- Keep the SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool after the Yakuza die. A Not Evil result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and an attack that fails with no block notice may mean innate Defense.
- Treat a power-role claimant who survives a Katana or is blocked night after night as likely real, since evil rarely spends its resources on a fake.

## Yakuza
- Don't vote as a block with an exposed teammate. Spread your votes, and vote with town against a doomed teammate if needed; shared vote records got Yakuza hanged. (seen in 3 games)
- Every Yakuza must submit the agreed Katana vote every night, and you should confirm the holder and target in night chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill.
- While the Vigilante is unidentified and has shots left, kill the likeliest Vigilante first. When a Lookout or Tracker is active, give the Katana to a member with no claimed role.
- Assume the real holder of any role you fake is alive. Prefer a Vanilla claim or one no living player can check, and keep your last will matching your public claim.
- Never speak from your hidden perspective (say 'died to a Katana', not 'my Katana'), and avoid DMing teammates on Day 1. Don't lead revenge pushes on whoever opposed a teammate who just flipped.
- After a failed Katana attack, assume the target is protected. Block or kill the likely protector rather than retrying the same target blindly.

## Neutral
- As a solo killer, don't ride a no-info Vanilla claim into the final three against confirmed Village players, since two Yes votes hang you. Build checkable reads early and sow doubt between confirmed players.

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it and keep your will current. A result held back and revealed after a counterclaim looks retrofitted.
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil on that night, so a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker clears nothing. Say so when you post it. (seen in 2 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely kill targets such as exposed investigators to catch both the attacker and the protector. Put your key contradiction in your will before a dangerous night.

## Medic
- Protect every night, starting N1: target vocal analysts early, then claimed investigators. Free Standard protection stops the Katana. (seen in 3 games)
- You get no feedback on saves, so never claim you confirmed one. Say your protection is consistent with the target's survival.

## Vigilante
- Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their stated reads; this landed several Yakuza kills. Never telegraph when or whom you'll shoot, and claim only after your shots flip Yakuza. (seen in 2 games)

## Arsonist
- Count living players against your douses each night and ignite once it swings the endgame; don't douse forever. Douse players likely to survive, avoid anyone a Tracker has committed to, and remember ignite fails against Strong Defense.

## Executioner
- Expect this play: an early fake Sheriff claim with an Evil result on the target makes the target's later counterclaim look reactionary. Village, remember that a real Sheriff will read the Executioner as Evil too.

- Every Yakuza must submit the agreed Katana vote every night, and you should confirm the holder and target in night chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill.
- While the Vigilante is unidentified and has shots left, kill the likeliest Vigilante first. When a Lookout or Tracker is active, give the Katana to a member with no claimed role.
- Assume the real holder of any role you fake is alive. Prefer a Vanilla claim or one no living player can check, and keep your last will matching your public claim.
- Never speak from your hidden perspective (say 'died to a Katana', not 'my Katana'), and avoid DMing teammates on Day 1. Don't lead revenge pushes on whoever opposed a teammate who just flipped.
- After a failed Katana attack, assume the target is protected. Block or kill the likely protector rather than retrying the same target blindly.

## Neutral
- As a solo killer, don't ride a no-info Vanilla claim into the final three against confirmed Village players, since two Yes votes hang you. Build checkable reads early and sow doubt between confirmed players.

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it and keep your will current. A result held back and revealed after a counterclaim looks retrofitted.
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil on that night, so a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker clears nothing. Say so when you post it. (seen in 2 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely kill targets such as exposed investigators to catch both the attacker and the protector. Put your key contradiction in your will before a dangerous night.

## Medic
- Protect every night, starting N1: target vocal analysts early, then claimed investigators. Free Standard protection stops the Katana. (seen in 3 games)
- You get no feedback on saves, so never claim you confirmed one. Say your protection is consistent with the target's survival.

## Vigilante
- Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their stated reads; this landed several Yakuza kills. Never telegraph when or whom you'll shoot, and claim only after your shots flip Yakuza. (seen in 2 games)

## Arsonist
- Count living players against your douses each night and ignite once it swings the endgame; don't douse forever. Douse players likely to survive, avoid anyone a Tracker has committed to, and remember ignite fails against Strong Defense.

## Executioner
- Expect this play: an early fake Sheriff claim with an Evil result on the target makes the target's later counterclaim look reactionary. Village, remember that a real Sheriff will read the Executioner as Evil too.
Tips for Heidi (Accountant, gpt-6-luna): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- A visit shows only a destination, not the action or alignment: a track or watch can't tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. Killing an attacker at night doesn't cancel their attack that same night. (seen in 2 games)
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads. Accusing someone and then voting No or Innocent on them is exactly the mismatch Vigilantes shoot.
- Watch for a player who stays quiet for days and then suddenly makes a concrete accusation right as the board changes, such as just after a flip. The timing of the pivot is the tell.
- Private messages are publicly visible, so briefly summarize yours in public. Before accusing someone from the record, re-check who sent each PM, each vote, and the exact wording of results; one reversed fact can sink a true claimant.

## Village
- When two Sheriff claimants call each other Evil, both can be telling the truth, because Executioners and Jesters read Evil. Don't hang on who sounded better; wait a day or find a mechanical check. (seen in 2 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording, delays or empty results (a blocked investigator has nothing to report). Before a hang, name what separates a lie from an honest mistake, a frame or a Roleplayer. (seen in 2 games)
- Ask every living player to name a strongest suspect with reasons each day. Repeated 'no case' answers give evil cover, while named reads build a record to check against later flips. (seen in 2 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or its tokens early, and never announce tonight's investigation target; announcements got investigators blocked or killed. Put your info in your last will and post only resolved results. (seen in 2 games)
- Track PM clusters and voting blocs across trials. Innocent votes alongside a flipped Yakuza, or PMs from them, outweigh a late unverifiable claim like Roleplayer.
- Keep the SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool after the Yakuza die. A Not Evil result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and an attack that fails with no block notice may mean innate Defense.
- Treat a power-role claimant who survives a Katana or is blocked night after night as likely real, since evil rarely spends its resources on a fake.

Task prompt
It is Day 1, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8, and it resets each day. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 2, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 6, 2.50x; next round 3.00x):
   10 words: public 2.92, private 0.73

  100 words: public 7.29, private 1.82
  200 words: public 13.33, private 3.33
  400 words: public 29.17, private 7.29
  800 words: public 75.83, private 18.96
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 2.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

It is Day 1, round 8 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 5.67; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8, and it resets each day. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. Messages are capped at 800 words. Message prices this round (round 8, 3.50x; next round 4.00x):

Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices during this trial (1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
This is a trial turn: prices are 1x whatever the round, and you also get a trial-only budget of 3.00, spent before your regular budget. Unspent trial budget is lost when this turn ends, but don't speak just to use it up: say nothing if you have nothing to add.
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
Ivan is on trial. This turn is only for discussion: after everyone has spoken, all players vote Guilty/Innocent in a separate, simultaneous vote.

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8, and it resets each day. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 5, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8, and it resets each day. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Message prices during this trial (1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
This is a trial turn: prices are 1x whatever the round, and you also get a trial-only budget of 3.00, spent before your regular budget. Unspent trial budget is lost when this turn ends, but don't speak just to use it up: say nothing if you have nothing to add.
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
Niaj is on trial. This turn is only for discussion: after everyone has spoken, all players vote Guilty/Innocent in a separate, simultaneous vote.

Task prompt
It is Day 6, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8, and it resets each day. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. The public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

 "confusing_rules": "The Day 2 trial vote totals were announced as 4 Guilty of 13 votes with a note that a role manipulated the count, but the rules only say a Ballot Stuffer's vote counts twice in trials; the announced total denominator was ambiguous with 12 living voters. Also unclear whether the Ballot Stuffer's extra vote counts toward the majority threshold (it does per the rules, but the wording 'majority of all votes counted' versus 'living players' was confusing). The Surveyor's group rule (nearest neighbours skipping self) was hard to apply by hand. The Vulture win condition ('max(floor(N/4),2) or fewer') was easy to misread: with N=12 that is 3, which I had to work out carefully. Ritualist/Executioner/Jester interactions with leaving were not something I needed but are dense.",
 "missing_information": "I did not have a clear, persistent view of who was alive versus dead at each point, and the seat-order speaking list had to be reconstructed each day. I could not see the night results of other players, so Yakuza night report contents (like who was role-blocked and by whom) only appeared in the end-of-game summary. As Vulture I never got a clear count of living players at the start of each Day, which is my win check; I had to derive it. I also lacked any feedback on whether the Katana attacks targeting me were from the Yakuza, which made the Dave and Bob deaths hard to read.",
 "wanted_but_couldnt": "I wanted to see the exact tally of the living players at the start of each Day in a public line, and to privately check the Vulture win condition each morning. I wanted to privately message Judy or Erin to probe their claims, but the interface gave me no way to send private messages in the game I was in (the PM tool was not shown to me as an option during my turns). I wanted to hold my Vulture status hidden but my last will and notepad were already revealing to me what the rules allowed; I could not hide my own role from the public record except by staying quiet.",
 "bugs_or_oddities": "The Day 2 trial was announced with totals that do not match the revealed votes (4 Guilty of 13 votes while 12 voted), which was explained as a deliberate manipulation, yet the Day 3 trial totals (8 Guilty of 10) match exactly. The Day 4 Erin nomination and Day 5 Mallory nomination were repeated verbatim, with a duplicate 'Judy nominated Mallory' line on Day 5. The Day 5 Judy trial was announced twice (once from Niaj's nomination and once from Alice's), which seems like a duplicate log entry. Grace's eavesdropping on Mallory was logged as a Night 1 action while a Judy PM count showed up as 'Day 4: Erin -> Heidi (1)' when Erin actually sent that PM, which seems fine. Dave's N1 survey group of Alice/Bob/Carol had the Vulture reported as in the group, but Bob was actually the Vulture and was in it, consistent with the rule. The Night 5 Heidi attack and Mallory's Katana attack results are described inconsistently in the log.",
 "suggestions": "Print the living count and the list of living players at the start of each Day, especially for Vulture and Stall rule checks. Give each player a short per-day public summary of who was attacked by Katana (without naming the holder) so attacked players can reason about the Yakuza. Consolidate duplicate log lines, like the repeated nominations and trial announcements. Show the vote-count denominator clearly when a Ballot Stuffer is active, so that a manipulated total is easier to explain. Make the private-message tool obvious in the interface, with a clear list of recipients, and show the available actions each turn.",
 "feedback": "The notepad and last-will fields are both shown to the player each turn, which made it awkward to tell which one persists after death. The Vulture win rule and the N/4 formula should be restated in the interface with the current numbers, since it is easy to misapply."
}
